newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico CPP, CCP and CCP-UDI rates fall Sept vs Aug.
newsitem.headline: Mexico CPP, CCP and CCP-UDI rates fall Sept vs Aug.

text.p: Mexico CPP fell 260 basis points in September from the month before to 24.92 percent, the Banco de Mexico said. The CPP, the average bank cost of borrowing from the public, was at 27.52 percent in month.
The central bank said that the CCP, the average bank term deposit cost measured in pesos in Mexican banks, was 25.84 percent for September against 28.58 percent for August.
The CCP will eventually become a substitute for the CPP, with the aim of better reflecting the cost of those term deposits for the banks, the central bank said.
The Banco de Mexico also said that the CCP-UDIs, the CPP measured in UDIs, an inflation indexed investment unit, was at 7.77 percent for the month, down from 7.98 percent in the month before.

The Banco de Mexico has said it publishes the various rates in order to give a better idea to the public of the cost of borrowing, and so that banks can only use the reference rates signaled by the central bank, which it hopes will better reflect market conditions.
